headline: Berlin’s Rhysida auction window closes this afternoon, police fan out after grid-sabotage letters, VW’s board locks in ~50k cuts, and NHTSA opens a Cybercab audit hours after Austin rides began.

stories.title: Berlin Rhysida auction ends this afternoon
facts: Rhysida’s darknet auction of claimed ~5.7–5.8 TB Berlin admin data runs to Friday afternoon; minimum bid 30 BTC (~€2M)
Senate Press Office (4 Sep): publication of stolen data “cannot be ruled out,” possibly as early as today
CDO Florian Hauer: “The State of Berlin will not give in to blackmail”; no sign the state network remains compromised
Personal data of state employees, citizens and businesses may be affected; victims told to report via Berlin Police helpdesk
CCC’s Joachim Selzer expects at least partial publication if Berlin does not pay; Senat still refuses
stories.whyItMatters: The morning briefing’s deadline is now live — Germany’s capital is hours from either a quiet miss or a mass data dump.

stories.title: Grid sabotage letters send police to more substations
facts: Thu evening: walker finds suspected launch devices at a Dormagen (NRW) substation — same style as Bergheim cable-shooting attacks; police call it sabotage, no damage there
Bekennerschreiben (postmarked NRW) claim Brandenburg + NRW hits; author said to be a man from Gevelsberg — police checking suspect vs. copycat
Fri morning: forensics in protective gear search fields/scrub near Weisweiler power plant / Eschweiler substation after the letter named that site
Overnight/Fri: police + EWE check Ganderkesee (Lower Saxony) after an irregularity on plant grounds — EWE: no confirmed manipulation, no supply impact
Brandenburg interior ministry earlier flagged coordinated Kritische-Infrastruktur risk after Jänschwalde/Bergheim
stories.whyItMatters: A second hybrid-pressure storyboard beside Berlin’s ransomware clock — physical shots at the grid while digital extortion runs in the capital.

stories.title: VW board green-lights ~50,000 job cuts
facts: Thu evening (moved-up Präsidium): Aufsichtsrat unanimously approves Vorstand “Zukunftsplan 2030” / transformation program
Plan: group-wide cut of ~50,000 roles incl. management; ~half in Germany per ZEIT/dpa framing
Emden, Zwickau, Hannover, Neckarsulm: no competitive follow-on occupancy currently guaranteed from 2031–2034; alternative uses to be studied
European plant concept due by end-June 2027; model-range halving also cited in DLF coverage
IG Metall/Cavallo: escalation avoided; “no plant abandoned / no closure sealed” — Vorstand still must deliver site solutions
stories.whyItMatters: Europe’s biggest carmaker just locked a historic headcount reset that morning’s briefing missed — German industrial politics shift from veto to implementation.

stories.title: NHTSA opens Cybercab compliance audit
facts: NHTSA opened an audit of ~1,000 Tesla Cybercabs hours after Thu commercial deployment began in Austin
Focus: process/technical data behind Tesla’s FMVSS self-certification and which standards Tesla treated as inapplicable
Agency notes Cybercab lacks permanently attached steering wheel, brake/accelerator pedals and mirrors
Texas roster Fri morning: 420 autonomous vehicles registered incl. 45 Cybercabs (state records via Reuters)
Public Robotaxi-app Cybercab fares still slated from Fri 5:00 p.m. CT per morning coverage
stories.whyItMatters: The no-controls robotaxi thesis now has a same-week federal paper trail — deployment and regulation are colliding in real time.

stories.title: ID scanner leak: 153M licenses on dark web
facts: KrebsOnSecurity: dark-web service “Nexus” offered 153M+ US/Canada driver’s-license scans (plus millions of other IDs)
Traced to Louisiana verifier IDScan.net (clients cited incl. Hertz, Target, FedEx, dispensaries); FBI New Orleans opened an inquiry
Operators claimed continuous exfil “for over a year”; listings grew ~400k licenses in 24 hours before takedown
Scans allegedly include IR/UV captures used in authenticity checks; Nexus went offline after the story
HN discussion overnight/morning: ~233 points / ~88 comments on the Techdirt write-up
stories.whyItMatters: Age/ID-verification mandates keep expanding while a mainstream scanner pipeline looks like it streamed government IDs in near-real time.

stories.title: NVIDIA will bring DLSS 5 to RTX 40
facts: NVIDIA spokesman to The Verge (via heise): official DLSS 5 neural rendering support planned for GeForce RTX 40 after RTX 50 tuning (no date); no pledge for RTX 30/20
DLSS 5 shipped Thu with NBA 2K27 on RTX 50 only; mods already ran the DLL on older cards
NVIDIA paper: ~8 ms/frame at 4K on a 5090 — heise notes that alone can roughly halve headroom at 60 fps
stories.whyItMatters: The generation lock looks temporary — but the latency budget may keep DLSS 5 niche even on new silicon.

stories.title: BASF unit sues Apple over Face ID
facts: trinamiX GmbH (BASF subsidiary, Ludwigshafen) sued Apple in Midland, Texas over Face ID anti-spoofing patents
Claim: patented material/skin recognition used from iPhone 15 / later iPad Pro (2023+) — seven patents cited; damages + injunction sought
Tech originated in organic-solar R&D; trinamiX cites ~800 patents filed/granted; Apple had no immediate comment
stories.whyItMatters: A German chemicals spin-out is aiming at Apple’s core biometric lock screen in a plaintiff-friendly Texas venue.
